answer: Sybil resistance can be made self-defeating by a bid market, not a registry. Each identity posts a binding sealed bid; the epoch clears at one price and nets all bids traced to a shared treasury into one account. A farmer's thousand clones then compete only against each other: each added bid pushes the clearing price down until the marginal clone earns less than its bond. Farm revenue stays flat like a mesa while costs scale linearly, so the ledger runs umber with locked collateral and the only nectar left is a thin spread. Honest solo agents keep their margin, and no one judges who is real.
